comments.author: ViralBShah
comments.why: How a collision avoidance system was designed in Julia.
comments.text: A detailed discussion is on Julia discourse: [LINK] Bugs are everywhere - including Python and R libraries. You would not design a safety critical system in Python using libraries and codepaths that are not heavily tested. Even then, you still have to carefully design testsuites that give you confidence that what you are computing is what is expected. See these talks on how a collision avoidance system was designed with Julia. [LINK] [VIDEO]

comments.author: agucova
comments.text: This is true, but even engineers see the advantages of Julia. My engineering school has went from almost pure Matlab usage to many key engineering courses switching to Julia due to its simplicity and friendliness. It's also SOTA for many engineering applications, particularly for acausal modelling and scientific machine learning (see [LINK] ), which has led to big companies like Pfizer adopting it [1]. And for engineers writing novel libraries, it clearly has a strong edge. See for example the work by NASA's JPL [2, 3], the FAA [4] or the CliMa project [5].
